question.problem:
A curve is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=4t\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{t}{\pi }),\,y=t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\in (0,\infty ).
$$

Let $C$ be the point that corresponds to $t=\pi $ on the curve. Determine the point at which the normal to the curve at $C$ crosses the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the coordinates of the point $C$ by substituting $t=\pi $ into the parametric equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4\pi \operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{\pi }{\pi })=4\pi (0)=0, \\ y & =\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi =-\pi \end{aligned}
$$

So we're looking to determine the equation of the normal at the point $(0,-\pi ).$ For this, we need to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ which means we first need to find the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ as follows:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=4\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{t}{\pi })+4,\,{y}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{t}{\pi })+4}.\end{aligned}
$$

At the point where $t=\pi ,$ the slope $m$ of the tangent line is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{dy}{dx}|}_{t=\pi } & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi }{4\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{\pi }{\pi })+4} \\  & =\frac{-1}{4\cdot 0+4}=-\,\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope ${m}_{n}$ of the normal line, we take the negative reciprocal of $m$:

$$
{m}_{n}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{\,(-\frac{1}{4})\,}=4
$$

To calculate the equation of the normal, we use point-slope form with the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(0,-\pi )$ and the slope ${m}_{n}=4.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(-\pi ) & =4(x-0) \\ y & =4x-\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The normal intersects the $x$-axis when $y=0.$ At this point, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-\pi  & =0 \\ 4x & =\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $(\frac{\pi }{4},0)$ is the $x$-intercept.
